config.population_budget_definition: min(0.02 * final coefficient-QCLE vs Schrodinger population difference, 0.5e-4)

checks.name: p10_refinement.exact_grids
checks.note: fine and coarse grids must be the pinned simultaneous two-axis refinement pair

checks.name: p10_refinement.same_physical_configuration
checks.note: the two runs may differ only in n_R and n_P

checks.name: p10_refinement.only_boundary_sentinels_fail
checks.note: all production checks other than the generic R/P edge sentinels must pass; unexpected failures: none

checks.name: p10_refinement.complete_matching_histories
checks.note: the complete saved population histories must share every time

checks.name: p10_refinement.finite_inputs
checks.note: all datasets used by the acceptance calculation are finite

checks.name: p10_refinement.population_history_change
checks.note: max population L-infinity change over the complete history; budget is tied to the physical comparison and table precision

checks.name: p10_refinement.boundary_R_reduction
checks.note: R-edge sentinel must fall by at least 16x; observed 54.1x

checks.name: p10_refinement.boundary_P_reduction
checks.note: P-edge sentinel must fall by at least 16x; observed 30.5x

checks.name: p10_refinement.fine_boundary_R_below_observable_budget
checks.note: the residual R-edge proxy must be below the declared population error budget

checks.name: p10_refinement.fine_boundary_P_below_observable_budget
checks.note: the residual P-edge proxy must be below the declared population error budget

checks.name: p10_refinement.opposite_R_edges_symmetric
checks.note: symmetric opposite edges identify a spectral floor rather than one-sided physical leakage

checks.name: p10_refinement.opposite_P_edges_symmetric
checks.note: symmetric opposite edges identify a spectral floor rather than one-sided physical leakage

results.interpretation: The original edge sentinels remain failed in the raw production archive.  The refined result is accepted for the reported population observable because simultaneous two-axis refinement collapses a symmetric Fourier floor and changes the complete population history by less than the declared numerical budget.
